introduction.title: Introduction to Codessa
introduction.description: Codessa acts as an intelligent layer between your repository and your developers. By automatically analyzing Pull Requests, it identifies structural flaws, style violations, and potential bugs before a human reviewer even looks at the code.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.description: Our engine doesn't just look at line-level syntax; it builds a localized semantic graph of your changes to understand how modifications impact surrounding files and architectural patterns.

step1.title: 1. Push Code
step1.body: Developer pushes a commit and opens a Pull Request in GitHub.

step2.title: 2. AI Analysis
step2.body: Codessa intercepts the webhook, fetching diffs and context for analysis.

step3.title: 3. Feedback
step3.body: Actionable comments and suggested fixes are posted directly to the PR.

ready.title: Ready to set it up?
ready.description: The Quickstart Guide walks through signing in, installing the app, and configuring review settings.

quickstart.title: Quickstart Guide
quickstart.description: Getting Codessa running takes a few minutes: sign in, install the GitHub App, enable AI review, then add a config file to tune how it reviews each repository.

setup.title: Get connected

step1.title: Sign in using GitHub
step1.body: Open the Codessa homepage and click Sign up. You'll authorize access through GitHub OAuth — there's no new password to create.

step2.title: Install the GitHub App
step2.body: From your dashboard, add a repository and install the Codessa GitHub App, choosing which account or organization and which repositories it can access.

step3.title: Enable AI review on a repository
step3.body: AI review is off by default. Find the repository in Overview and toggle its status from Disabled to Enabled.

setup.enabledDesc: Enabling is per repository — turn it on for some and leave others off. Once enabled, every new pull request is reviewed automatically.

config.title: Configuration Setup

description.prefix: After enabling a repository, add a
description.suffix: file to the root of that repository. This is where Codessa reads how strict to be, which language to write in, and what to focus on.

config.pushDesc: Push the file to your default branch and it takes effect on the next pull request — nothing is re-reviewed retroactively.

fields.auto_review: When true, every new pull request is reviewed automatically.
fields.language: Language used for review comments: en, id, or zh.
fields.tone: Writing style of the review: friendly, strict, or concise.
fields.review_rules_ignore_paths: Glob patterns for files or folders Codessa should skip.
fields.analysis_focus: Turn security, performance, bugs, and code_style checks on or off individually.
fields.severity_threshold: How strict Codessa is about failing the commit status: critical_only, balanced, or strict.
fields.custom_instructions: Free-form extra instructions for the AI reviewer.

description.prefix: A repository's review behavior can come from three places. Codessa checks them in order, field by field, so a
description.suffix: file doesn't have to set everything to take effect.

precedence.title: How precedence works
precedence.description: For every individual setting — tone, severity threshold, each analysis focus flag — Codessa looks top to bottom until it finds a value.

tier1.title: .codessa.yml
tier1.subtitle: Committed to the repository
tier1.desc: Any field set here wins, no matter what the dashboard says. It lives with the code and travels with the branch, which makes it the most specific place to configure a repo.

tier2.title: Dashboard Settings
tier2.subtitle: Set per repository in Codessa
tier2.desc: Used for any field .codessa.yml leaves out. Handy for a quick baseline without maintaining a config file at all.

tier3.title: Built-in defaults
tier3.subtitle: Shipped with Codessa
tier3.desc: Used when a field isn't set in .codessa.yml or the dashboard. Every repository always ends up with a complete, working configuration.
